source_text: Nunc igitur ad eum, quicum agimus, sermo respiciat. Acquiescis legi Dei (professione interim, ceterum, quid facias argumentando, novimus), an resistis? Si acquiescis, sublata contentio est, si resistis, sublata consensio est; si acquiescis, exstincta Traducianorum, si resistis, Manichaeorum revelata perfidia est, dummodo constet opinioni vestrae et legi Dei neutiquam convenire.
pass_a_gloss: Now therefore let speech look back to him with whom we deal. Do you acquiesce in the law of God (by profession meanwhile; otherwise we know what you do by arguing), or do you resist? If you acquiesce, the contention is taken away; if you resist, agreement is taken away; if you acquiesce, the unbelief of the advocates of inherited sin is extinguished; if you resist, the unbelief of the Manichaeans is revealed, provided it stands that your opinion and the law of God by no means agree.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Traduciani=those who teach tradux peccati; not merely traducianism of the soul
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: Now, then, let my words address the man with whom we are disputing. Do you submit to God’s law—at least in your profession, for we know what you do in argument—or do you resist it? If you submit, the dispute is over; if you resist, our agreement is over. If you submit, the error of the advocates of inherited sin is extinguished; if you resist, the unbelief of the Manichaeans is exposed. At all events, it stands established that your opinion and God’s law cannot agree.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian's label for teachers of tradux peccati. Keep the polemic name as a description of transmitted sin, not as a theory of the soul's origin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
